Rashi on Chullin 105b:10:1.english: The angel of poverty was pursuing him - [The] angel appointed over poverty was pursuing [him] to trap him and bring him to poverty:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:10:2.english: [Over] grass - upon grasses that are in the meadow:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:10:3.hebrew: נפל לידאי - שלא יוכל ללקט הפירורין מבין העשבים, ויהו למדרס רגלים, ואלכדנו בכך:
Rashi on Chullin 105b:10:3.english: He will fall into my hands - [For] he will not be able to gather the crumbs from among the grass, and they will be [left] to be trampled underfoot, and I will ensnare him through this.

Rashi on Chullin 105b:10:4.english: He heard him - That man [heard] that angel:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:10:5.english: [That] he was saying: "Woe, that he removed him from his house" - This [man] has removed me from my resting place:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:11:2.english: For karsam [catarrh] - Mucus that comes from the nose:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:11:3.english: Pushing it aside - with his hand to the sides:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:11:4.english: He should sink it - into the beverage until it dissipates on its own:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:12:1.english: For catarrh of wine - [meaning] that which comes upon him because of the foam of wine:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:12:2.english: Beer - Its remedy is to drink beer:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:12:3.hebrew: לכרסם דשכרא - שבא מחמת אופיא דשכרא, לישתי מיא:
Rashi on Chullin 105b:12:3.english: For catarrh of beer - [that is, catarrh] that comes on account of the foam of beer, he should drink water:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:12:4.english: After the poor man - this [refers to one] who had only water to drink:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:13:1.english: From a bundle tied by the gardener - [meaning] that one does not pull out garlic or leeks from a bundle that vegetable sellers tie, in order to eat it:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:13:2.english: Like gluttony - for he cannot wait until he unties it:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:13:3.hebrew: לכשפים - הרואה אותו יכול לעשות לו כשפים, והנשמר ממנו אין כשפים נוחין לחול עליו:
Rashi on Chullin 105b:13:3.english: For witchcraft - One who sees him can perform witchcraft against him, whereas [for] one who guards himself from it, witchcraft does not easily take effect upon him:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:14:2.english: Seat me with you - Seat me with you on the boat:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:14:3.english: She said something - [meaning] an incantation of witches:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:14:4.english: She bound the boat - so that it did not move from its place:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:14:5.hebrew: אמרי אינהו מילתא - אף הן היו בקיאין בדבר, ועושין להציל עצמם מיד המכשול. ואיכא דאמרי שאמרו שם, ולא מוכחא מילתא:
Rashi on Chullin 105b:14:5.english: They said something - They too were knowledgeable in the matter [of incantations], and acted [accordingly] to save themselves from harm. And some say that they recited a [Divine] Name, and the matter is not clear:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:14:6.hebrew: מאי איעבד לכו - שאין מכשפות שולטת בכם, שאתם נשמרין מכל דבר הקשה להן:
Rashi on Chullin 105b:14:6.english: What can I do to you - [meaning] that witchcraft has no power over you, because you guard yourselves from everything that is harmful to them [witches]:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:14:7.hebrew: דלא מקנח לכו בחספא - אין אתם מקנחין עצמכם בחרס בבית הכסא, ואין אתם הורגין כינה במלבושכם:
Rashi on Chullin 105b:14:7.english: As you do not wipe yourselves with an earthenware shard - You do not wipe yourselves with an earthenware shard in the privy, and you do not kill a louse on your garments:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:15:1.english: A gutter [marziva] - a pipe that pours water from the roof:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:15:2.hebrew: שופכין - שמא ירדו עליו מים מאוסין המקלחים מתשמיש המשתמשין על הגג, ושופכין מי תשמיש, והן באין לצינור:
Rashi on Chullin 105b:15:2.english: Waste water - lest repulsive water fall upon him, streaming from the activity of those using the roof, who pour out waste water and it comes into the gutter:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:16:1.english: Porters [shakul’ei] - Carriers of loads for hire:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:16:2.english: [The barrel] burst - For the demon broke it:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:16:4.hebrew: דאותביה באונאי - הושיבוה באזני, שהייתי ישן שם:
Rashi on Chullin 105b:16:4.english: That they placed it on my ear - They placed it on my ear, as I was sleeping there:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:17:1.hebrew: דצייר וחתים - כלומר, באחד מכל אלו אין לנו רשות:
Rashi on Chullin 105b:17:1.english: That is tied up and sealed - That is to say, with [any] one of all these, we have no authority [to take from it]:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:18:1.english: That they pour out water - One who drinks from a pitcher first pours some of the water onto the ground:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:18:2.english: Because of twigs - splinters and bits of straw that are on the surface of the water:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:18:3.hebrew: מים רעים - פעמים ששתה מהן שד, וזו תקנתן:
Rashi on Chullin 105b:18:3.english: Foul waters - Sometimes a demon drank from them, and this is their remedy:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:19:1.english: That was in [the house of] Rav Pappa - [meaning] that it was serving him:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:19:2.english: Until the foul waters passed - [waters] from which the demons had drunk:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:1:1.hebrew: סולדת - נכוית. אם היד סולדת בהן, בטלו ונשתנו מתורת מים:
Rashi on Chullin 105b:1:1.english: Recoils - [is] scalded. If the hand recoils from them, [the waters] are nullified and have changed from the status of water:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:2:1.english: There are those who teach it with regard to the latter clause - they only taught that final [waters may] not [be washed] with hot [water]:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:2:2.hebrew: מכלל כו' - דבהנך דאסר לאחרונים, שרי לראשונים:
Rashi on Chullin 105b:2:2.english: By inference, etc. - For with those [hot waters] that [he] forbade for final [waters], it is permitted for first [waters]:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:4:1.hebrew: שמלח סדומית יש - ואמרו חכמים: "על כל אכילתך אכול מלח", וכיון דנגע במלח, כי הדר יהיב ידו אעינים, מסמא להו, ולפיכך צריך לנטלן:
Rashi on Chullin 105b:4:1.english: Because Sodomite salt is present - And the Sages said: "With everything you eat, eat salt," and since one touches the salt, when he later puts his hand on [his] eyes, it blinds them, and therefore one must wash them [one's hands].

Rashi on Chullin 105b:4:2.english: And it is found like a pinch in a kor - It is only found [at a ratio of] a pinch in a kor:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:4:3.hebrew: כל מילחא - מדד מלח, כמו (שמות ט״ז:י״ח): "וימודו בעומר" — ומתרגמינן "וכלו בעומרא":
Rashi on Chullin 105b:4:3.english: Measured salt [kal milcha] - [Kal means] he measured salt, as [in the verse] (Exodus 16:18): "And they measured [vayimodu] with an omer," [which Targum Onkelos translates as] "and they measured [vechalu] with the omera":

Rashi on Chullin 105b:4:4.english: What [is the halakha] - Must one wash [his hands] after it, or not?

Rashi on Chullin 105b:5:1.english: Due to messiness - because their odor is foul and they appear repulsive:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:6:1.hebrew: למישתי - כשאדם שותה, אין לוקחין כלום מלפניו:
Rashi on Chullin 105b:6:1.english: To drink - When a person is drinking, one does not take anything from before him:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:6:2.hebrew: דבר קלקלה - שמא יכעוס השותה, שחפץ באותו דבר הניטל, וכי יכעוס — יסתכן ויחנק:
Rashi on Chullin 105b:6:2.english: A mishap - Lest the drinker become angry, because he wanted that item that was taken, and when he becomes angry, he will be in danger and choke:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:7:1.english: Beyond four cubits - That one takes it out beyond four cubits of the table:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:9:1.english: That [people] collect the crumbs - that they sweep crumbs of food from the house:

Rashi on Chullin 105b:9:2.english: Mankiruta [cleanliness] - To clean the house; cleanliness:

Tosafot on Chullin 105b:3:1.hebrew: לא שנו אלא בין תבשיל לתבשיל - אומר רבינו שמואל דמיירי בשניהם של בשר או שניהם של גבינה, אבל בין תבשיל של בשר לגבינה שלפניו חובה; אבל לגבינה של אחריו לא קאמר, דאפילו בנטילת ידים אסור לאכול עד סעודה אחרת, כדאמר לעיל: אכל בשר, אסור לאכול גבינה. ואין נראה לר"ת, ד"בין תבשיל לגבינה" משמע תבשיל תחלה, כדאמר לעיל: כמה ישהה בין בשר לגבינה? ולא כלום! ופריך: והא אמר רב חסדא, אכל בשר, אסור לאכול גבינה! אלא כמה ישהה בין גבינה לבשר כו'. ועוד: בין תבשיל לתבשיל, בשניהם של בשר או של גבינה, למה יש לו ליטול כלל? ומפרש ר"ת ד"בין תבשיל לתבשיל" היינו בין תבשיל דבשר לתבשיל של גבינה, דכיון דאין הבשר והגבינה בעין וליכא אלא טעם, לא החמירו שיהא חובה ליטול ידיו בינתיים, ואינו אלא רשות; אבל בין תבשיל דבשר לגבינה, שהגבינה בעין, חובה. ויתכן פירוש זה אף לדברי האוסרין לאכול גבינה אחר בשר באותה סעודה אפי' בנטילה וקינוח:
Tosafot on Chullin 105b:3:1.english: They taught [this] only between [one] cooked dish and [another] cooked dish - Rabbeinu Shmuel says that it is speaking [of a case] where both of them are of meat or both of them are of cheese; however, between a cooked dish of meat and cheese [eaten] before it, [washing] is obligatory; whereas [regarding] cheese [eaten] after it, he does not say [so], for even with washing of the hands it is forbidden to eat [cheese after meat] until another meal, as [the Gemara] said above: "[If] one ate meat, he is forbidden to eat cheese." But this does not seem [correct] to Rabbeinu Tam, for "between a cooked dish and cheese" implies [that] the cooked dish is first, just as [the Gemara] said above: "How long must one wait between meat and cheese? Nothing at all!" And [the Gemara] objects: "But did Rav Chisda not say: [If] one ate meat, he is forbidden to eat cheese! Rather, how long must one wait between cheese and meat, etc.?" Furthermore: between [one] cooked dish and [another] cooked dish, where both of them are of meat or of cheese, why should one have to wash at all? Rather, Rabbeinu Tam explains that "between [one] cooked dish and [another] cooked dish" means between a cooked dish of meat and a cooked dish of cheese; for since the meat and the cheese are not [present] in substance and there is only taste, [the Sages] were not stringent that it should be obligatory to wash one's hands in between, and it is only optional; whereas between a cooked dish of meat and cheese, where the cheese is [present] in substance, [washing] is obligatory. And this explanation is plausible even according to the words of those who forbid eating cheese after meat in the same meal, even with washing and wiping:
